title: How to get a second phone number: 4 options compared (2026)
summary: Learn about four ways to get a second phone number, what each actually costs, and how app-based numbers differ from a cellular second line.
body_markdown:
Ever wish you could separate work and personal calls without carrying two phones?


You might want one to keep your personal number private when using your phone for business calls. Or maybe you need a dedicated[business number](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-business-phone-number/) entirely.


There are four ways to get a second phone number, and they come down to two technologies. You can get a second phone number through a cellular carrier or a virtual phone provider. Cellular carriers offer second phone numbers through a second SIM card or an eSIM. Virtual phone providers offer virtual numbers that use the internet to transmit calls and texts. They also offer additional features that can save businesses time. Virtual numbers let you make calls[without a SIM card](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-call-without-sim-card/) .


In this article, you’ll learn about the ways you can get a second phone number. If you’re looking for a[second phone number app for Androids](https://www.quo.com/blog/second-phone-number-android/) or iPhones, you’ll also find a list of must-have features to look for.


##


How a second phone number works


A second phone number is an additional number that works on your existing device. It works just like your primary phone number. The only difference is how you make calls and texts with it.


You can make calls with a second phone number in two ways: **internet and cellular.**


**Voice over Internet Protocol, or VoIP, numbers** make calls and send texts over the internet. They convert voice signals into digital packets and use an internet connection to facilitate conversations. These numbers don’t require an extra SIM card and they can work across multiple devices simultaneously. They’re virtual numbers since they aren’t tied to a physical device.


**Cellular numbers** make calls over traditional cell networks. Similar to your personal number, they require a SIM card to connect to a carrier network. Cell numbers are a great option if you need a second number for personal use. However, they aren’t the best option if you need to share a second number with your team.


Scroll down to learn about the different ways you can get a second phone number in minutes.

##


**Four ways to get a second phone number**


Here are a few popular options for getting a second phone number and how they stack up:


Method Best for Cost Pros Cons


Free apps Personal use or temporary needs $0–10+ per month No upfront cost, quick setup Ads, limited features, unreliable for business


Dual-SIM phones Heavy phone users or those with dual-SIM preference $10–100 per month Works with data, easy to use Requires compatible phone, managing two plans, limited business phone features


Second number with existing cell carrier Individuals who want a business number with their carrier $10–50+ per month Unlimited calling and texting in the US, Mexico, andCanada Limited business features, can lock you into expensive contract, also requires dual SIM


Business virtual phone apps Small and growing businesses $15–50+ per month Business features, team collaboration, scalable Internet-dependent, some expensive providers


Here are a few more details on each of these options to help you decide:


### **1. Free apps: Best for personal use**


If you’re looking to try a second phone number, a free app is a solid option to see if it’s right for you.


Free apps like TextNow or 2nd Line work fine if you don’t mind ads and don’t need to keep the number long-term. They’re great for keeping your real phone number private when using Facebook Marketplace or dating apps. They help you block spam calls and telemarketing notifications, too. You can pick and choose temporary numbers based on your needs. You aren’t tied to a single number for the long term.


The problem with free apps is they aren’t built to scale. If you want to use a free phone service for your business, you’ll quickly find they fall short. You can’t share your second number, split responsibility for incoming calls and texts, or integrate with third-party apps. You should also know that free doesn’t always mean *free* . When TextNow shows you ads between your calls, it slows down your productivity. If you don’t want ads, you have to upgrade to its paid plan.


### **2. Business virtual number apps: Best for businesses**


Business virtual phone apps are ideal if you need to share phone numbers with your team. They’re also a great option for managing customer relationships and scaling communications as you grow.


Teams usually realize they need a business virtual phone when they invite their colleagues. Free apps don’t let teams share the same phone number. You can’t collaborate on incoming calls and texts.


With business virtual phone apps, your team communicates with customers using the same phone number. They can use their existing devices to access business virtual phone apps. They just need to log in to your workspace to start making voice calls.


Free apps and carrier add-ons don’t have call routing, shared inboxes, CRM integrations, or other tools businesses depend on. That’s where business phone apps step in. The best part is they’re available at a low cost. For example, Quo starts at $15 per user per month.


**Already have a second number?** You can move your number to a business virtual phone to continue using it. Free apps don’t let you port your existing numbers.[Port your existing number to Quo](https://www.quo.com/porting) to keep the number your customers know while upgrading to business features.


### **3. Second number with existing carrier: **Best for separating work and personal numbers****


If you run a business in an office and want to bundle your phone and internet plan, this option can work for you. Internet providers like AT&T and Verizon offer deals on their phone and internet plans. You can get multiple phone lines at a discount with your internet plan.


Alternatively, you can add a second phone number to your existing mobile plan. Verizon provides this through its Second Number offering, which starts at $10 per number per month. You pay for it as an additional line item in your monthly phone bill.


The drawback of this approach? Cell carriers offer limited features in these types of second phone numbers:


- **No collaboration features.** They don’t prioritize features like shared numbers or CRM integrations.
- **No AI summaries and transcripts.** Teams have to take notes manually, which adds work during calls.
- **No AI voice agents.** They don’t offer 24/7 voice agents, which leads to missed calls after business hours.


Another drawback is that this option often requires a dual SIM capable device. With Verizon Second Number, this is an explicit requirement to make use of this feature. This can limit your ability to add a second number if you don’t already have this type of device.


### **4. Dual SIM phones: Best for a second personal number**


If you want two phone numbers but don’t want to deal with ads, a dual SIM phone is for you. They mimic the experience of having a second personal number. What makes this option different from the previous one is you can combine SIM cards from different providers in the same device. Then you can add a second physical SIM to your dual SIM device. Many smartphones now let you add multiple SIMs to your phone with eSIMs.


The drawback with dual SIM or multi-SIM phones is similar to free apps: they aren’t built for business communications. You can’t share dual SIM or eSIM numbers with your team. You also can’t view your team communications in a shared inbox or log calls and texts with your CRM. It also lacks automated texting and any advanced AI features.


##


Dual SIM vs virtual phone apps: Which one should you choose?


Now that you know how each second phone number option works, you might be considering which one to choose.


Virtual phone apps work across multiple device types. Your team can use their existing devices to access your business phone. You can also access business-friendly features like AI call summaries and transcriptions, internal threads, and automated text messages.


Dual SIM phones offer none of this flexibility. You can’t share them with your team. You also can’t access any of the business-friendly features that come with virtual business phone apps.


If you’re looking for a second phone number for personal use, consider a dual SIM. If you already have an eSIM-compatible phone, this option is a no-brainer. But if you need a second phone number for business use, go with a virtual phone app. It’s the option that will scale with your team’s growth.

Plus, with separate contact books, you’ll know which phone calls are personal and which are for work. This way, you’ll know exactly how to respond to every incoming call.


For example, when a Quo contact calls you, you know that it’s a work call in your caller ID. No more guessing the context behind a call. You can answer calls with confidence and pick up the conversation where you left off.


### **2. Balance work and personal time**

### **3. Share your business number with your team**


When you rely on your personal phone, only you can answer calls. This makes it hard for your team to help when you’re busy. Getting a separate business number with providers like Quo means you can split the responsibility with your staff.


[Shared numbers](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-share-a-business-phone-number-with-your-team/) let you:

- **Give everyone on the same number visibility into conversations** so nothing gets missed or repeated. As the team grows, you can[give each person their own line](https://www.quo.com/phone-numbers/multiple-phone-lines) too.
- [Use one phone number on two phones](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-use-one-phone-number-on-two-phones/) so you can stay flexible with who handles calls and when.


### **4. Minimize spam and robocalls**


Second phone number apps like Quo let you set up[IVR](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-ivr/) to[screen calls](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management/call-screening) and filter spam and robocalls. That’s because these automated callers can’t navigate phone menus.


On Quo, you can also add spam callers to your blocklist. Quo blocks numbers across your entire workspace so you can stomp out robocalls for your whole team.


Looking for more ways to block spam calls? Here’s a deep dive from the FTC on


[blocking unwanted calls](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-block-unwanted-calls) .


### ****5. Replace your landline****


Landlines may be reliable, but they come with major limitations. You’re stuck in one location, you may pay expensive long-distance fees, and you can’t text customers. A virtual second phone number solves all three problems while letting you and your team work from anywhere.

##


**Is a second phone number private and safe?**


Depending on your personal experience with second phone numbers, you might wonder if they’re safe to use. After all, if you get a temporary phone number for free, can you be sure that your call and text data isn’t being sold to the highest bidder?


Here are the most common questions we get about second phone number data privacy and security:


**Is a second-number app safe?** Safety depends on the provider and how they make money. A free, ad-funded app makes money from your usage. A subscription provider makes money from your monthly subscription. You should know which one you’re using before you put customer conversations through it.


What separates a business provider is verifiable rather than promised. That includes encryption in transit and at rest, an independent security audit, and a data-handling policy you can read before you sign up.


**Can someone look up who owns the number?** Some second-number providers market anonymity as a feature, meaning the number is not tied to your name or billing details. That’s useful if you have a temporary number.


For a business number, it’s usually the opposite of what you want. You want your business number to be tied to your business name and identity. Business providers can program their caller ID so customers can recognize them when a call comes in.

****FAQs****


****How do I get a second phone number for free?****


Services like Google Voice offer virtual personal phone numbers for free. Here’s how you can get one:
1. **Sign in:** Go to voice.google.com and sign in with your Google account.
2. **Select numbers:** Select available phone numbers by area code. Google also suggests a local phone number for you based on your location.
3. **Verify existing number:** You have to link an existing phone number to your Voice account for identity verification. Share your phone number, receive a verification code, and enter the code to continue.
4. **Finish setup:** Click Finish to start using your free Voice number.
Google Voice’s free version has several limitations to keep in mind. **** These include zero customer support, no toll-free numbers, not being available in Canada, and not being able to set business hours. Google Voice is meant more for personal use.


Fortunately,[Google Voice alternatives](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-alternatives/) offer the features your business needs.


**How long does it take to get a second phone number?**


Virtual phone providers can help you get a second number in minutes. If you get a second SIM, you might have to spend additional time purchasing a dual SIM phone or setting up eSIM on your existing phone.


**Who uses a second phone number?**


Curious about why solo operators and teams get a second phone number? Here are some reasons why a second phone number can be useful:
• **Solo operators.** Solopreneurs use a second phone number to separate their work and personal calls. When they get a call, they know why someone might be calling and can respond accordingly. Their work calls have a separate call history and their business number may have dedicated routing features to help them manage incoming calls.
• **Home service businesses.** If you’re managing a trade business, a second phone number is useful to handle new customer requests. You can automatically send appointment reminders and updates when a technician is almost at their location. Second phone numbers can integrate with a field service platform like Jobber so you don’t have to send updates manually.
• **Law firms.** Legal practices have an overwhelming number of calls to manage with every case. How can they keep track of every conversation without losing specific details? With a second phone number’s automatic call recording and call transcription, they don’t have to manually take notes. Every conversation is logged and can be referenced when the team needs it.


****Can you have two phone numbers on one cell phone?****


You can use a virtual number app like Quo to have[two numbers on one mobile phone](https://www.quo.com/blog/2-phone-numbers-on-1-phone/) . Your existing number will continue to work for personal calls. Your new number — dedicated to business — will function through the app.


******How does a second phone number app work without a SIM card work**** ?**


Since calls and texts travel over your internet connection rather than a cellular network, you don’t need a SIM card to use second phone number apps like Quo. Instead, they use VoIP technology to route your calls and texts over WiFi. You choose a new number, then use it on your phone, computer, or tablet through the app or desktop version.


Simply open the app to make calls or send messages — just like you would with a regular phone number. VoIP services eliminate the need for an extra device, mobile data plan, or to[change your number](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-change-phone-number/) .


**Do second phone numbers show up on my phone bill?**


Yes, second phone numbers can show up on your phone bill. If you pay for a second number in your carrier’s plan, it may show up as an additional line item. If you pay for multiple numbers with a business phone provider, it might not show up as an individual line item in your bill.


****Can I use second phone numbers for international calls?****


Yes, you can make international calls with many second phone number apps. Make sure to check their rates so you know upfront how much calls and texts cost.

**How do I set up a second phone number on my iPhone?**


It’s easy to set up a secondary number on your iPhone with Quo:

2. Choose your new phone number.

After that, simply download the Quo app from the App Store, and you’re ready to make calls, send texts, and manage both numbers from one device.


****Do second number apps integrate with other business tools?****


Integrations depend on the second number app. For example, Quo integrates natively with HubSpot, Salesforce, and Jobber, and connects with Zapier and Make to automate workflows with thousands of other tools.


****Can I use a second phone number for verification codes like 2FA?****


If your primary goal with a second phone number is for verification, then you shouldn’t get a VoIP phone number. Banks, rideshare apps, and some social platforms check whether a phone number is registered to a mobile carrier before sending verification codes. It’s a fraud prevention measure to prevent spam accounts from being created. If you need a number specifically to receive verification codes, a cellular number is the more reliable choice.


****What are the legal implications of using a second phone number?****


There are a few regulations you’re required to follow to use a virtual second phone number. The FCC requires that businesses adhere to the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, or TCPA.[TCPA compliance](https://www.quo.com/blog/tcpa-compliance-checklist/#tcpa-compliance-checklist-rules-and-best-practices-to-follow) requires businesses to collect opt-in consent for any customer communications. You’re also required to honor opt-outs responsibly.


You must also comply with A2P 10DLC requirements. A2P 10DLC refers to Application-to-Person messaging; major telecom carriers pushed for these guidelines. It helps improve your text message deliverability rates.


[A2P 10DLC compliance](https://www.quo.com/blog/10dlc-compliance/) requires a multi-step application process that you can complete in your Quo dashboard. The average approval time is five to seven days, but some applications can take up to two weeks.
